tables.concept: Outcome entity (likely user/account). One row per entity with a creation/signup timestamp and several categorical attributes.
Hierarchical objects owned by the entity (e.g. workspaces/projects and child items). Exactly one type-1 root row per entity, created at the entity's signup time; type 2/3 rows reference a parent row.
High-volume activity/usage event log recorded against T06 objects, with an event-type code and a numeric magnitude.
Paid subscriptions: at most one per entity, with a plan code, a status code, a start timestamp and a nullable cancellation timestamp. Possibly the source of the conversion milestone.
Billing/invoice line events per subscription, recurring roughly monthly. Has a type code and a signed amount, apparently in minor currency units.
Entity-level interaction records (e.g. support tickets, feedback or issues) with a type code and an optional 1-5 rating. Optionally tied to a T06 object; has two timestamps.
Scheduled lifecycle/onboarding message sequence per entity (steps 1-8), with two binary engagement flags such as opened and clicked.
Small 40-row lookup referenced by T05.c06. Possibly country/locale, with a region group and a UTC-offset-like value.
Plan/pricing tier dimension: 6 plans, each with a price and a capacity quota.

columns.meaning: Activity/event type code (15 values).
Reference to the T06 object the event occurred on.
Numeric magnitude of the event (whole numbers 100-115377), e.g. duration in ms or size; matches no key.
Event timestamp.
Subscribed plan code, referencing T09.c04.
Subscription status code. Value 2 (729 rows) matches exactly the 729 non-null cancellation timestamps, so 2 likely means cancelled; 1 likely active; 3 another state (e.g. past due/paused).
Subscription start timestamp; also the first T04 billing timestamp.
Subscription primary key.
Entity (T05) that owns the subscription; unique, so at most one subscription per entity.
Cancellation/end timestamp (null while active).
Second timestamp of the record, typically after c07 (e.g. resolved/updated time).
Record type/category code (4 values).
Optional reference to the related T06 object.
Optional 1-5 rating/score (roughly uniform, 40% null), e.g. satisfaction or severity.
Entity (T05) the record belongs to.
Record primary key.
Creation timestamp of the record.
Subscription the billing line belongs to.

Billing line type. Types 1 and 3 have identical counts (25360, equal to the distinct timestamps), suggesting paired lines such as charge and payment per cycle; 2 is likely an extra charge and 4 a rare refund/credit.
Signed monetary amount, likely in minor currency units (e.g. 7900 ~ plan price 79). Negative values may be payments or refunds.
Billing timestamp; recurs at ~30-day intervals from subscription start.
Billing line primary key.
Entity creation/signup timestamp.
Entity primary key (the outcome entity).
Entity attribute code (4 values, skewed), e.g. segment or signup source.
Entity attribute code (6 values). Overlap with T09 plan ids is possible but unproven (e.g. plan of interest), more likely an independent category such as company size.
Entity attribute code (7 values), e.g. acquisition channel.
Reference to T07 lookup (40 values, full coverage), e.g. country.
Object creation timestamp; type-1 rows coincide with the entity's signup time.
Object type/level. Type 1 occurs once per entity (20000) as the root; types 2 and 3 are children.
Parent object id (self-reference). Null share 23.6% matches the 20000 type-1 root rows.
Owning entity (T05).
Object primary key.
Grouping code (5 values), e.g. region/continent.
Signed small integer (-9 to 10), possibly a UTC offset or score.
Lookup primary key (1-40).
Plan tier/family group (5 values over 6 plans).
Plan capacity quota (3 to 500), e.g. seats or projects.
Plan primary key (1-6).

outcome_insights.statement: The total count of T01 activity events on an entity's T06 objects is the strongest single predictor; higher counts are associated with conversion.
The model (logistic regression, test AUROC 0.746) clearly beats the best single past-activity count baseline (0.570). Multi-table activity features carry predictive signal.

More T03 records (via the entity or via its T06 objects), especially T03.c02 = 1, are associated with a lower conversion rate. If T03 holds support tickets or problems, friction may co-occur with non-conversion.
Specific T01 event types differ: type 4 counts are associated with conversion (AUROC ~0.66), while type 11 counts are associated with non-conversion (AUROC ~0.42).
More recent T06 object creation (fewer days since last) and more T06 objects/children are associated with conversion.
T08 message counts carry no signal (AUROC 0.5), consistent with a fixed schedule. Only the engagement flag rate (mean T08.c03) shows a weak positive association.
Static T05 attributes are only weakly associated with conversion.
The conversion milestone is probably the start of a paid subscription in T02 (one per entity, ~21% of entities), so T02/T04 must be excluded from features to avoid leakage.

ambiguities.description: Whether the conversion milestone equals the T02 subscription start, or another event.
Small-integer codes match both T07.c03 and T09.c04 coincidentally. Only T02.c01 -> T09.c04 and T05.c06 -> T07.c03 seem plausible; T05.c04 -> T09.c04 is unresolved.
Business meaning of T03 (tickets, feedback, errors?), its type codes, the 1-5 rating, and the two timestamps.
Meaning of T01.c03 (duration, size, count?) and of the 15 T01 event types.
Semantics of T04 line types and the amount sign/currency unit.
T07 content: is c02 a UTC offset or a score, and c01 a region?
Whether a T03 record's T06 object always belongs to the same entity as T03.c05. The two paths (P:path:2 vs P:path:3) may count different records.

next_investigations: Check whether each label positive coincides with a T02.c03 subscription start within 16 days of the cutoff, to confirm the conversion definition and rule out leakage.
Validate T02.c02 = 2 against non-null T02.c06 row by row, and profile T04 amounts by type against T09 prices for the plan.
Obtain the dictionary of T01.c01 event types (especially 4 and 11) and T03.c02 types from product owners.
Test consistency: does T06(T03.c03).c04 equal T03.c05, and does T06(T06.c03).c04 equal T06.c04?
Add recency/window features (e.g. T01 counts in the last 7/16 days, T01 count normalised by account age) to separate activity intensity from tenure.
Check whether T08.c04 equals T05.c01 plus a fixed offset and step-based days, confirming a scheduled drip; test open/click flags at earlier steps as engagement signals.
Confirm the meaning of T05 attribute codes and the T07 lookup with the business.
